sections.html:
A direct cash sale gives the shortest wait before closing. A listing takes longer and rewards a house that shows well. Selling on your own is the third route, and it suits owners who have the time and a good title company.

Oswego is a village on the Fox River in Kendall County, with a small part in Will County. It is the largest municipality in Kendall County, with 39,948 residents, up 15.4% from 34,585 in 2020. Most of the housing went up in the building boom that began in the mid-1980s and pushed the village west of the river, so buyers tend to ask about roofs, windows and mechanical systems first.

  • Hire an agent if the roof, windows and mechanical systems are in good order and you can handle showings and a financing timeline.
  • Handle the sale yourself if you can price the home from recent nearby sales and coordinate the paperwork the village requires.
  • Take a cash buyer if the house needs work, is vacant, or belongs to an estate. Weigh the offer against a listing price after commission, repairs and the months of taxes and utilities you would carry.

A cash buyer takes the house as it is, so you skip the repair list that usually follows a buyer's inspection, and you skip the wait for a lender's appraisal and approval.

Oswego voters approved a real estate transfer tax on June 28, 2022. The buyer pays it at $3 per $1,000 of the sale price. A stamp from the village is required before the deed can be recorded with Kendall or Will County, even when the buyer is exempt from the tax.

The seller still has a part in the process, because open village bills block the stamp. Here is the sequence:

  1. The buyer or a representative sends a MyDec or PTAX-203 declaration at least three business days before closing, online or at Village Hall.
  2. The village prepares a Statement of Open Accounts. Any open invoice tied to the property must be paid in full before the stamp is released.
  3. After review, the buyer brings the deed to Village Hall at 100 Parkers Mill, open weekdays from 8 a.m. until 5 p.m., and the tax is calculated while they wait.
  4. Payment is accepted by credit card, cash or certified check.

A person who has owned a primary residence in Oswego for at least a year is exempt when buying another Oswego home, but still obtains a stamp. The money goes to the water and sewer fund, tied to the Lake Michigan water connection through the DuPage Water Commission. Questions go to TransferTax@oswegoil.org or (630) 554-0864.

As the seller, check your water and sewer account early and pay anything outstanding. A small unpaid invoice is the most common thing that can hold up a stamp and push back the closing date.

sections.h2: How are Kendall County property taxes billed?
sections.html:
Kendall County mails one bill a year and collects it in two installments, in June and September. A late payment is charged 1.5% of the installment per month. Call the Collector for the exact dates on your bill.

The Collector's office is at 504 S. Main Street in Yorkville, open weekdays from 8 a.m. until 4:30 p.m., with the telephone at 630-553-4124. The county will not take estimated or partial payments, so the exact amount on the bill is required. It accepts payment online, by phone, by ACH, by mail, at most Kendall County banks, and in person, and a drop box outside the office is available at any hour.

Get a copy of the bill from the Collector. At the closing table, the title company splits that year's tax between you and the buyer by the days each of you owned the house, so you want the real figure in hand ahead of time. If your house is in the part of Oswego that lies in Will County, the bill comes from that county instead.

Oswego handles residential permits through its Building and Permits department, and a long list of projects needs one. The village's application list covers basement remodels, decks, driveways, fences, fireplaces, garages, hot tubs, HVAC, irrigation systems, patios, pergolas, permanent pools, sheds, solar, sump pumps and downspouts, and window and door replacement.

Roof, siding, radon and water heater permits go through an online portal called Civic Access. The other applications are emailed to the department. If you did work on the house, gather the permit and final inspection records for the buyer, since a roof or window replacement with no permit on file is the sort of gap an inspector asks about, and a missing record can stall a closing that is otherwise ready.

Floodplain rules apply along the river and creeks. Any change to a structure in the floodplain may need a permit, and the substantial improvement rule generally limits an addition to less than fifty percent of the structure's value. The village has a floodplain map where you can check an address, and it asks owners to contact it before designing a project.

sections.h2: Which school district is your house in?
sections.html:
Oswego Community Unit School District 308 serves most of the village, and portions of Oswego fall within Yorkville Community Unit School District 115. Because District 308 also reaches Boulder Hill, Montgomery, Plainfield, Aurora, Yorkville and Joliet, the attendance zone is not always obvious from the village name. Confirm the district for your address before listing, and name the nearest elementary and junior high on the flyer.

The closing for an Oswego sale follows a plain order. The buyer's side files the declaration, the village reports any open accounts, you pay what is owed, the village releases the stamp, and the deed goes to the county for recording. Nothing in that order needs the house to be repaired, which is one reason owners with a vacant or inherited property choose a cash buyer who can work around the village's timing.

A short list of what to have ready when you sell: the tax bill, permit and inspection records for any work, receipts for sump pump or drainage work, and the water and sewer account number.

Owners live in 87.9% of Oswego homes, so most sales are owner to owner, and typical buyers are families who will want a clean inspection.

faqs.q: Who pays the Oswego real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: The buyer. The tax is $3 per $1,000 of the sale price, and a village stamp is needed before the deed is recorded. The seller's part is clearing any open village invoices on the property.

faqs.q: How early must the transfer declaration reach Oswego?
faqs.a: At least three business days before closing. Send a MyDec or PTAX-203 to the village online or at Village Hall, and the village will then prepare its Statement of Open Accounts.

faqs.q: Is anyone exempt from the Oswego transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners of an Oswego primary residence for at least one year are exempt when they buy another home in the village, though they still need a stamp.

faqs.q: When are Kendall County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Kendall County issues one bill, payable in two parts in June and September, and charges 1.5% per month on late payments. Call the Collector at 630-553-4124 for the dates on your bill.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a roof in Oswego?
faqs.a: Yes. Roof permits are filed through the village's Civic Access online portal. Keep the permit and final inspection record to hand to the buyer.
